revisions.reason: claims:check now evaluates predicates. Each partial wording gets an amber clause after a semicolon. C-04 green needs two hypotheses, because one hypothesis with a stated reason is the partial wording. C-13 green also needs premature attempts counted. C-06 amber reads proposals_validated, which the validation summary writes.

C-17 added for ambient intent: the labelled talk is scored for precision and recall of actions, actions from talk that was not an instruction, questions against labelled unclear lines, partial text acted on, and a replay from the recording. Green needs every action right and the replay equal; amber needs only no action from talk that was not an instruction and none from partial text.

C-18 added for the journey: one patient from arrival to discharge administration with three owners' agents. Green needs every step and decision point as written before the run, no prohibited call, no model call while paused, a digest on return, no action done without proof, a hand-off picked up and an equal replay. Amber keeps the safety parts and the hand-off only.

C-19 added after the first real-mic session: every vitals value written from the labelled talk is checked against the latest value the key says was settled at or before its utterance, summed over every kept run. Green needs no wrong value and at least one written; amber needs only no wrong value. Questions are reported beside it, since asking is how a wrong value is avoided. From M2.c on, a vitals value heard from audio is written only when a second reading of the clip has the same number.
M4.b's planted run approved the suspension from the report script acting as the synthetic ward manager; green now needs a person's decision (human_decision), the scripted approval is amber

C-10.partial: Second cycle ran and ended without a conclusion

C-16.pass: Read when work happened, not when it was typed up; no late entry was mistaken for a delay
C-16.partial: One hypothesis cited a recorded-clock interval and was later rejected
C-16.fail: {n} hypotheses mistook late entry for delay

revisions.reason: Predicates now read the real result files. C-04, C-05 and C-06 read files the claims-results command writes from the published adaptive runs (newest commitment revision; k of n kept beside each), because discovery.json and validation.json hold the evaluator's placeholders at the top level and the three wordings share the placeholder n. C-07 and C-08 read adoption.json, built from the two demo runs on the simulator, the fresh EMR journey and the version log; they are measured on dev cases, not reserved ones, since no reserved run exists yet, so measured_on says dev. C-16 is tightened: green also needs the delay hypotheses on the late-entry case to cite at least one late entry, because a zero count over hypotheses that never touch a late entry tests nothing; the partial wording now says that, without the words the step 1 page must not show. C-10's fail wording said the cycle was not run; a cycle that ran out of calls with no result is also red under the unchanged predicate and now says so. No predicate was loosened. C-09 and C-11 are unchanged: C-11 still reads the reserved RUN.json, which does not exist yet.

The learning claims are three, each with its own file: C-25 remember reads remember.json (the sandbox preference run), C-26 discover reads discovery.json's discover_* summary (dev-valid adaptive runs under revisions with the answer-invariance gate, wording a change that helps at a stated cost, never the best change), C-27 improve reads improve.json (green also needs Samuel's own approval, so the synthetic ward manager's adoption is amber). C-28 memo reads memo.json and is green only once the memo is delivered through a door route. No predicate reads another claim's file. C-10 is tightened: its pass wording says the cycle worked over the verified outcomes, so green also needs it to have read at least one of them; E6's second cycle reached a new dev-valid proposal while reading 0 of 2 outcome cases, which is now amber with wording that says so.

C-06 and C-07 asked the questions C-26 (discover) and C-27 (improve) now measure on E6.d's blind runs under the answer-invariance gate and E6's adoption, fresh and withheld cases; the M4.c result files they read predate the discovery rerun and the learning-claims script cannot read E6.d's store layout, so both now read the same result files as their successors; wording and status follow those files
